A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we show that the current privacy budget is too small to make the deep learning models perform better than the traditional handcrafted models, and we also show that if the privacy budget is increased, deep learning models will perform much better.
we demonstrate that differentially-private machine learning has not reached its ''Alexnet moment''.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the performance of private machine learning will not improve significantly until the community can develop a better understanding of what features should be learned by a model trained on private data.
we need to improve the features we learn in order to make differentially private learning more effective.
